sentence: This project studies where HIV hides in the central nervous system and lymphoid tissues and builds T cell therapies to suppress it.
This project builds real-time imaging that tracks heart motion so proton radiation therapy can treat a heart rhythm disorder more safely.
This project supports genetics and genomics research that answers basic questions about human biology and disease.
This project tests how glial cells in the aged mouse brain can be converted into functional neurons and maps the steps.
This project builds an AI tool that gives education and support to rural care partners of people with Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementia.
This project studies the molecular steps that control stem cells and regeneration in planarians.
This project tests whether fecal immune, metabolic and microbial data can predict severe illness, treatment response and recurrence of Clostridioides difficile infection.
This project uses clonal barcoding and single cell genomics to find genes that drive metastasis and chemoresistance in ovarian cancer.
This project studies how chronic drug use changes lipid signaling molecules in plasma, the central nervous system and breast milk.
This project tests whether a therapy that blocks an inflammatory pathway can protect myelinated axons in progressive multiple sclerosis.
This project tests an extended-release RNA-based therapy to stop fibrotic changes in disc cells and restore disc structure in a large animal model.
This project studies how cannabis use changes alcohol craving and consumption in people early in treatment for Alcohol Use Disorder.
This project uses machine learning to understand what drives dietary decisions and tests a personalized incentive platform for healthy food purchases.
This project studies how a regulator called Chronophage keeps intestinal stem cells in quiescence and protects the gut during aging.
This project studies how a protein involved in neuronal signaling switches on microglia in Alzheimer's disease.
This project studies malaria mosquitoes and parasites in sub-Saharan Africa, using molecular biology, bioinformatics and modeling to help control the disease.
This project builds a reporter system that uses bacterial transporters to track genome-edited immune cells in the body with nuclear imaging.
This project studies which cell types and contexts matter for a disease by combining single-cell data with genome-wide association studies.
This project acquires a liquid chromatograph triple quadrupole mass spectrometer to measure biomolecules, metabolites, biomarkers and contaminants.
This project builds computational models that map how interacting proteins, DNA and RNA shape cell behavior and how 3D genome folding works.
